Metadata.title: AirClaims — claim your flight compensation yourself
Metadata.description: Delayed or cancelled flight? Claim up to €600 under EU261 yourself, with AI help. You only pay if you get paid.

Home.title: Your flight was delayed or cancelled? Claim up to €{long} yourself.
Home.subtitle: We prepare your claim, track the airline's answers and tell you what to do next. You stay the claimant and the money goes straight to you.
Home.amountMedium: 1,500 – 3,500 km, or longer within the EU
Home.amountsNote: Per passenger with a paid ticket, when you arrive {hours} hours late or more, or your flight is cancelled at short notice. Extraordinary circumstances (such as severe weather) can exempt the airline.
Home.step1Body: Flight number, date and what happened. We estimate if you're entitled to compensation.
Home.step2Body: We draft your claim. Nothing is sent to the airline until you read it and approve it.
Home.step3Body: The airline pays you directly. If they refuse, we guide you to AESA and, if needed, to court.
Home.feeTitle: You only pay if you get paid
Home.feeBody: {base}% of the compensation you receive, VAT included. Lower with more passengers, previous claims or referrals (never below {min}%). Expenses you get back are never charged.
Home.honestyBody: AirClaims is an assisted self-claim service. We are not a law firm and don't represent you: you are always the claimant, we never hold your money and we never accept an offer on your behalf.
Home.scorecardBody: Coming soon: how each airline responds to claims, based on real cases.

Forwarding.title: Get {airline}'s emails into your claim
Forwarding.intro: This airline replies to your own email address, not to your claim address. Forward its emails to your claim address and we'll read them, tell you what they mean and help you reply.
Forwarding.onceBody: When an email from the airline arrives, forward it to your claim address. Any mail app works.
Forwarding.filterTitle: Or set it up once: a filter
Forwarding.filterBody: Create a rule that forwards only emails from {domain} to your claim address. Nothing else from your inbox reaches us.

gmail.name: Gmail
steps: Open Gmail on a computer > Settings (gear) > See all settings > Forwarding and POP/IMAP.
Click "Add a forwarding address" and enter {alias}.
Gmail sends a confirmation code to that address: we'll forward it to you by email within a few minutes. Enter the code in Gmail.
Go to Filters and Blocked Addresses > Create a new filter. In "From" write {domain}.
Click "Create filter", tick "Forward it to" and choose {alias}. Save.

outlook.name: Outlook / Hotmail
steps: Open Outlook.com > Settings > Mail > Rules > Add new rule.
Name it (e.g. Airline claim). Condition: "From" contains {domain}.

icloud.name: iCloud Mail
steps: Open iCloud.com > Mail > Settings (gear) > Rules > Add a rule.
If a message "is from" {domain}, then "Forward to" {alias}.

Forwarding.privacy: We only use forwarded emails for this claim. We check that forwards really come from your mailbox before reading them.

help.title: How a claim works
help.intro: Every claim goes through these stages. Not every claim needs all of them: many end as soon as the airline pays.

stage.prepare: Tell us about the flight, what happened, the passengers, expenses and documents. We estimate what you are owed, then you sign.
stage.send: You submit the claim to the airline: through its web form (we give you the text and the steps) or by email from your claim address, after you approve it.
stage.airline_wait: The airline has one month to answer. Forward us anything it sends; we read it for you.
stage.airline_reply: The airline answered: paid, rejected, asked for documents or offered something else. We explain it and help you reply. You decide; we never accept anything for you.
stage.aesa_file: If the airline doesn't answer within a month, or you still disagree, you can file with AESA, free of charge, within one year of your claim to the airline.
stage.aesa_wait: AESA reviews both sides and decides, usually within 90 days. For flights from 2 June 2023 its decision binds the airline.
stage.closed: The claim ends paid, partly paid, rejected or withdrawn. You can withdraw at any stage.

paid.title: The airline pays
paid.body: The most common happy path: the airline accepts the claim and pays. Record it here and the claim is closed.

rejected.title: The airline says no
rejected.body: Often a generic reply (e.g. "extraordinary circumstances"). Airlines must say what happened and prove it: we help you ask for the proof. If it still says no, go to AESA.

formRefusal.title: The airline's form refuses automatically
formRefusal.body: Some web forms show "not eligible" right away. Take screenshots: it counts as the airline's answer, and you can reply and go to AESA.

offer.title: The airline offers a voucher or less money
offer.body: You don't have to accept. EU261 compensation is paid in money unless you agree otherwise in writing. We help you decline and ask for the full amount.

noAnswer.title: The airline doesn't answer
noAnswer.body: After one month without an answer you can go straight to AESA. You can also send a reminder first.

aesaIgnored.title: AESA agrees with you but the airline doesn't pay
aesaIgnored.body: You can go to court with AESA's decision. Under €2,000 it's a simple procedure (juicio verbal) and you don't need a lawyer.

lost.title: AESA agrees with the airline
lost.body: The claim closes as rejected. You can still go to court if you have new evidence.

help.disclaimer: General information, not legal advice. Deadlines and amounts follow EU Regulation 261/2004 as applied in Spain.

aesa.summary: I've filed the claim with AESA
aesa.body: Filed with AESA through its website? Tell us the date and reference so we can track its deadline.

outcome.body: Record only what actually happened. If the airline offers a voucher or less than you are owed, don't record it here: tell us its answer and we'll help you reply.
